summary.text: Ibadan was a war camp that became a city: a military republic where rank came from war, called the ‘gun base’. Its army stopped the jihad at Osogbo in 1840 and then built an empire in the east.

arms.text: A warrior class dominated the city; its chiefs rose by merit in war.
Ibadan was nicknamed the gun base.
Subject towns in the east, ruled through resident agents (ajele).

record.text: At Osogbo Ibadan decisively beat the jihad’s push south.
The Kiriji war ended in a stalemate, and a peace brokered from Lagos.
